why: Writes the `00 09 00 00` DELIMITED_CDR2 encapsulation header and starts the payload at origin 4. RFC-0055's XCDR2 DELIMITED_CDR2 machinery. The RFC carries a CORRECTION dated 2026-07-26 that refutes its own premise: a default Jazzy peer serializes FINAL/XCDR1 on the wire, DDS-XTypes REJECTS an appendable writer against a FINAL reader, and #0267 turned out to be two Cyclone descriptor-builder bugs rather than a DHEADER gap. So the path is built, tested and PARKED -- `nros-c/src/cdr.rs`'s `const XCDR2: bool = false` makes every one of these a compile-time no-op today, waiting for a per-type `@appendable` signal that nothing yet emits. ROS 2's equivalent is not an API at all: extensibility is a property of the IDL annotation and the middleware acts on it, so there is no rclcpp/rclc verb to correlate with. The asymmetry is deliberate and worth stating so it is not read as a gap: there is no `CdrReader::new_with_header_xcdr2`, because the READER detects the version from the header byte it is already parsing (`0x00|0x01` -> Xcdr1, `0x08|0x09` -> Xcdr2, cdr.rs:427). A writer has to be told; a reader is.
